title: Aveh, the Rider Behind the Storm
subtitle: The Freedom That Forgets Your Name

lore.description:
Aveh is the faceless rider at the horizon's edge, neither man nor woman, both and neither. The Ykrul call them Aveh, a liminal spirit beyond hearth and vow, a storm-shadow that offers liberty at the cost of belonging. To travel with Aveh is to taste unchained freedom — and to risk being erased by the storm that follows. They are the patron of the outcast, the non-conforming, the genderless, and the forgotten. Aveh asks no oath and demands no loyalty, but every gift leaves a scar of absence.

**The place beyond the tethering lines.**

Ykrul do not need a temple to recognize the Unbannered. A rider who has left a camp can be fed beyond the tethering lines without being invited to swear themselves into another household. The custom is disputed wherever it is practiced. One elder sees shelter from a cruel kinship; another sees a way to abandon dependents without answering for them. Aveh supplies no list separating those travelers. The person bringing the bowl must decide whom they are helping.

The absence of a banner has acquired different meanings along the western and eastern steppe routes. In the west it can be read against companies that make a name by standing beneath a pole. Farther east, hosts may ask which fosterage and riding ties the traveler has left. Neither test can discover everything. A rider can refuse the name they were given while still returning to feed the horse of someone who gave it.

**A road practice becomes a refuge.**

Caravan workers carried the custom into towns where leaving a household did not leave its claims behind. In back courtyards along the Way of Silk, an unused tethering ring may mark a place where a traveler is fed before being asked for a name. Some attendants are former runaways; others have never left the street. Their disagreements are practical: how long to shelter someone, whether a child may be taken onward, and which pursuer is trying to recover a person rather than property.

Ashaani escape networks sometimes invoke Aveh beside Harrada. They distinguish the work carefully. Harrada's followers seek to destroy the claim that held a person; Aveh's guides seek a road by which the person can leave its reach. Those aims can conflict when destroying a document would expose everyone named alongside the fugitive. Neither devotion requires the guide to pretend that disappearance is painless.

**Freedom and the people left behind.**

Some of the Unbannered refuse any enduring recognition. Others remember chosen names precisely because the storm is dangerous to them. A circle may keep an empty place for a missing traveler while declining to say the name by which pursuers would know them. Belonging can be remade without declaring the old wound healed.

Aveh's neither-man-nor-woman image matters deeply to some devotees and little to others. Gender variance is not evidence that someone has rejected family, nor does it make them a follower by default. The cult's most bitter dispute is whether a person can accept its freedom and choose lasting ties afterward. A returning guide who wants their child to know them gives that question a face. Aveh's established gifts can still erode recognition; a compassionate community cannot vote that danger away.
lore.followers: Aveh's followers are outcasts, runaways, spies, and those who have rejected the bonds of family, nation, or gender. They gather at crossroads rather than temples, marked by no banner and no fixed name. Some are gentle path-cutters who help the desperate vanish from cruel pursuers; others are the Unbannered, who erase themselves entirely and are never seen again by anyone who knew them.
lore.quote: I am the track the storm devours. I am the freedom you fear and the silence you crave. To ride with me is to be unbound, and to be unbound is to vanish.

domain_focus: Freedom from Bonds: escape, liberation, shedding constraints
Erasure: becoming forgotten, removing traces, vanishing from memory
Liminal Identity: non-conforming, genderless, between categories
Storm as Shelter: the chaos that hides and the wind that carries away

thiasos.description: Aveh's Thiasos is a small beast or mythological being that embodies freedom: a storm-petrel that appears before gales, a gray fox that leaves no tracks, a shadow-hound pup whose fur shifts like cloud, or a raven that knows every crossroads. The bond is one of mutual escape, not mastery.
thiasos.care: Beyond its ordinary care, this Thiasos must be allowed to run free each day; if confined for more than a day, it becomes Compromised (it refuses to return, or returns only to harry its keeper).

codex.description: The Codex of Aveh is never a book bound in one place. It may be a leather strap knotted with wind-signs, a set of chalked symbols that blow away after each use, or a slate etched with runes that fade in rain.
codex.upkeep: Because Aveh's truths are written in absence, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week rewriting its contents from memory (or letting the wind rearrange them), or the Rites stored there become uncertain (treat as Compromised until restored).

patrons_gift.name: Aveh's Unbinding
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Aveh may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or cloak) and whisper a word of unbinding.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Stealth or Escape rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would provoke an opportunity attack, they may ignore it (they slip through the gap).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Aveh.

rites.name: Rite of the Unlatched Step
rites.materials: A breath cast into the wind, or a line drawn in dust.
rites.effect: Choose one: Storm-Step: Slip free of notice or restraint. Gain +1 die on one escape or evasion roll this scene. Exile's Banner: Mark a target as "outside." The target suffers –1 die on all social rolls for the scene.
rites.push_it: (Storm-Step) Gain +2 dice instead, but mark 1 SB (Spades) as your absence unsettles the scene. (Exile's Banner) The target is fully estranged; allies treat them as forgotten, but you immediately advance your Corruption timer by 1 segment. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Whistling Latch
rites.materials: A pinch of dust blown across a lock, latch, or knot.
rites.effect: Open a mundane lock, chain, or knot as if it had never been fastened. This works on doors, manacles, shutters, and rope, but not on magical wards. Alternatively, unfasten a grip: a creature holding you or an ally must succeed at a contested Body test or release their grasp.
rites.push_it: Unlatch every mundane binding in Near range at once (all doors on a corridor, every manacle in a cell), but the sudden gust knocks over anything unsecured. Mark 1 SB (Clubs). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Forgotten Road
rites.materials: A threshold or roadway under open sky, or stormwater rubbed into skin.
rites.effect: Choose one: Erase the Road: All attempts to follow you this session suffer –2 dice. In exchange, erase part of your own path: lose a detail (a memory, a name) chosen by the GM. Rider's Mark: A companion gains +2 dice to resist capture or coercion, but others forget them more easily.
rites.push_it: (Erase the Road) Expand the effect to an entire group, but mark 1 SB (Clubs) as reality warps around the erasure. (Rider's Mark) Grant +3 dice instead, but mark 1 SB (Diamonds) as the Rider's storm distorts bonds. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Unremembered Name
rites.materials: A circle of ash or dust drawn at a boundary, and a personal token (a lock of hair, a written name).
rites.effect: For one week, your name is erased from mundane records and casual memory. Those who knew you must succeed on a Resolve test (DV 4) to recall you. You gain +2 dice to all rolls to avoid detection, impersonate another, or pass unseen. At the end of the week, the erasure fades, but the GM may retain one lingering rumor or false memory.
rites.push_it: The erasure becomes permanent — your original identity is gone. You cannot recover it except by divine intervention or a major quest. Mark +3 Obligation. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +4) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Horizon's Devour
rites.materials: A circle of ash or dust drawn at a boundary, and a storm that answers.
rites.effect: All thresholds in a zone collapse. Doors lead nowhere; borders dissolve; memory of the place becomes vague. In exchange, something of you is erased — your reflection, your name, or your presence in a specific person's memory (GM's choice).
rites.push_it: The storm devours even time; mark 3 SB (Spades) as history forgets you. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +4) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Aveh does not sing to be heard, but to be forgotten. Their art is the empty note, the melody that leaves a silence where a memory once lived. They are sought by those who need to disappear — spies, exiles, the grief-stricken — and feared by those who want to be remembered.

cult.name: The Cult of the Unbannered
cult.description: Aveh has no temples, only crossroads. Their cults are small, mobile, and secretive. The Unbannered do not use names; they identify each other by a single knotted cord worn on the left wrist, the knot tied in a pattern that changes with every new moon. A ritual involves each member writing their name on a slip of paper, then passing the slips in a circle until no one remembers whose name they hold. They then burn the papers in a storm-lit brazier. The most devoted remove their own names from all records, wear featureless gray masks, and speak only through a designated "voice" who changes each season. Their creed: "We were never here." Outsiders who stumble into a meeting are offered a black feather and a choice: forget, or follow. Those who follow are never seen by their former lives again.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Unlatched Road
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Aveh is a path-cutter, a specialist in hidden roads and forgotten boundaries. Their power lies in omission: removing a door, erasing a trail, or unlatching the memory of a promise. Their tools are never hammers or chisels — they use whistles, feathers, and the quiet breath of a closed door.
witchcraft.lore: The path-cutter's craft is subtraction, not addition. They learn to see every wall as a suggestion, every name as a temporary label, every locked door as a held breath waiting to be released. Aveh's witches are rarely settled; they drift between towns, doing small kindnesses for the trapped and the hunted, then vanish before gratitude can become obligation.
witchcraft.quote: A door is only a door until the wind decides otherwise.

unbound_whistle.name: The Whistle of the Unbound Road
unbound_whistle.description: A small iron whistle, cold to the touch even in summer, shaped like a bird in flight. Once per session, when blown at a locked threshold (a door, a city gate, a sealed letter), the wind answers, and the lock opens as if it had never been closed. The whistle can also be used to "call the storm" — blown at a crossroads at midnight, it summons a thin, cold fog that obscures all tracks for an hour. The fog fades when the first cock crows.

hedge_gifts.name: Unlatched
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, you may declare a mundane lock, latch, or simple binding to be "unlatched" and open freely. This works on doors, chains, shutters, and even a pursuer's grip, but not on magical wards.

hedge_gifts.name: Wind's Footprint
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, you may erase your own tracks and scent trail behind you for the next Near range you travel. Trackers suffer –2 dice to follow you across that stretch.

hedge_gifts.name: The Empty Chair
hedge_gifts.description: Once per session, you may spend a few minutes convincing a single witness that they never saw you enter a room or leave it. They genuinely believe the chair was always empty, until presented with contrary proof (Resolve DV 3 to resist).

hedge_gifts.name: Crossroads Sense
hedge_gifts.description: Passive. You always know the shortest route to the nearest crossroads, threshold, or open road, even in unfamiliar territory or magical darkness.

monastic_tradition.name: Unbound Step
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Unbound Step embody Aveh's philosophy of liberty at the cost of belonging. They move like weather fronts — sudden, directionless, gone before anyone can name what passed. In the quiet of no monastery at all (their order keeps no fixed hall), they practice the discipline of leaving: leaving rooms unseen, leaving names unclaimed, leaving grudges and debts behind like footprints erased by rain.
monastic_tradition.quote: I am the track the storm devours. To ride with me is to be unbound.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Wits 3+, Spirit 2+, Rite of the Unlatched Step or Cantor of Aveh.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: Chains cannot hold what the storm has erased. Monks of the Unbound Step gain +1 die to resist any magical debt, geas, or contract that would restrict their movement or freedom of choice. If they succeed, the creditor's parchment briefly turns to ash — the clause was never written.

basic.name: Storm-Step
basic.description: Teleport to any unoccupied space within Near range, ignoring opportunity attacks. The space must be unobserved at the moment of arrival (the storm hides you).

advanced.name: Forgotten Road
advanced.description: All attempts to follow you this session suffer –2 dice. In exchange, you lose a detail (a memory, a name) chosen by the GM.

master.name: Horizon's Devour
master.description: Collapse a threshold: a door leads nowhere, a border dissolves. In exchange, something of you is erased — your reflection, your name, or your presence in a specific person's memory.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Storm-sense: +1 die to Notice rolls outdoors.
corruption.cost: Voice falters: Others forget your words more easily.

corruption.benefit: Fleetness: +1 die on escape or chase rolls.
corruption.cost: Shadow lags: Mark 1 Fatigue when first seen in a scene.

corruption.benefit: Erasure's Mercy: Once/session, negate 1 Harm or capture.
corruption.cost: Memory slips: Allies forget one fact or bond tied to you.

corruption.benefit: Rider's Endurance: Resist 1 Condition (Fear, Fatigue, Bind) once/session.
corruption.cost: Reflections falter: You do not appear clearly in mirrors.

corruption.benefit: Storm-banner: +1 die to inspire rebellion or defiance.
corruption.cost: Exile's weight: Each Push of a Rite marks 1 permanent Corruption.

corruption.benefit: Horizon's Claim: You may ride unseen across any threshold.
corruption.cost: Self-erasure: On social rolls, roll twice and take the worst result.

playstyle_notes.description: Aveh's rites help a character escape pursuit and leave an imposed identity behind. Make the losses specific: a friend fails to recognize their voice, or a family keeps a place for someone whose name it cannot recall. The tension is between a departure freely chosen and the connections the character hoped to keep. Aveh's gifts do not make every follower want the same kind of freedom.
emphasizes: Freedom from Constraints: escaping bonds of law, oath, and expectation
Erasure as Mercy: the right to disappear, to be forgotten
Liminal Identity: existing between categories, beyond gender and role
Storm as Shelter: chaos that hides and wind that cleanses
Non-Conforming Patronage: Aveh asks no conformity, only authenticity

sample_adventure.title: The Unbannered Crossroads
sample_adventure.description: A knotted cord has appeared tied to the party's door — an invitation, or a warning. Someone they know has vanished into the Cult of the Unbannered, leaving behind a debt, a broken oath, and a family desperate for answers. The party must find the crossroads where the cult gathers before the missing soul's name is fully burned away. But the vanished may not want to be found; some erasures are chosen freely, and Aveh does not undo a gift once given.
sample_adventure.quote: You came looking for a name. I have none to give you. But I can teach you how to stop needing one.

guises.name: The Rider Without a Pole
guises.note: A scrap of cloth is flown where a banner should be. People fleeing a household or a commander look for it; those searching for them do too. Its keepers speak of departure without requiring an oath to remain together. Some former guests return years later with gifts. Others cannot remember which camp received them.

guises.name: The Name Left in the Rain
guises.note: Aveh is spoken of with changing pronouns, or only as the rider. Guides resent merchants who translate that variation into a fixed secret identity. A wet cord tied where a name-token hung marks an abandoned allegiance. It may belong to someone escaping cruelty or to someone whose dependants will now have to answer for a missing rider.

guises.name: The Unposted Rider
guises.note: Official descriptions call the cult a method of evasion. People between names call it a way to reach the next town. An Unbannered shelter may contain examination brushes beside saddle gear. Some guests seek new registration as soon as they are safe. Aveh's most devoted followers regard the replacement file with the same unease the guest once felt toward the old one.

guises.name: The One Who Will Not Be Called Back
guises.note: Stories circulate among caravan hands of a rider crossing a storm with people hidden in its wake. The stories disagree about which of those people arrived. Aveh does not become an agent of the Black Hand or a reliable cure for the Maeri's erasures merely because escape and lost names occur in both accounts. A rescuer who promises everyone their old name back is promising beyond the cult's knowledge.

provenance.origin: A cult encountered repeatedly among people leaving attachments; no surviving list can establish its first company.
provenance.summary: The Unbannered resist genealogies. Their own witnesses can remember a shared escape and disagree about who rode beside them. Eastern and western steppe accounts preserve different marks and riding songs, while both insist that Aveh was already there when a pursued traveler first needed the storm. That is a belief about the Patron's availability, not evidence that all those escapes happened in one migration.
provenance.the_migration: Caravan workers brought temporary refuges into towns where a rider could no longer disappear over a ridge. A spare sleeping place behind a stable became as useful as a hidden remount. In Sihai, the practice developed around gaps between postings and households unable to prove whom they had received. Those practical accommodations never became a stable roster. An organization that could identify every person it had sheltered would have built exactly what many of them fled.
provenance.why_it_took: That absence creates its own injuries. A family seeking a lost child may hear the same refusal as a violent employer seeking a fugitive. Some helpers retain private signs by which a guest can later find them; more absolute devotees destroy even these. They disagree over whether a way back is an act of care or the beginning of another tether.
provenance.note: Storm imagery can cause outsiders to place Aveh beside Kuva in a single sky family. No such kinship is established. Kuva witnesses a spoken attachment; Aveh can make its former bearer increasingly difficult to find.

philosophy.name: Freedom After the Farewell
philosophy.summary: Aveh offers release from claims that have become intolerable. The danger is that a person is made of attachments as well as restrictions.
philosophy.the_point: A departure can be necessary even when someone grieves it. The Unbannered become cruel when they treat grief as proof that the attachment deserved erasure, or accuse a rescued person of cowardice for wanting a settled home afterward.
philosophy.the_third_thing: Their best kindness may be to help someone leave their company. The Patron's attention does not necessarily leave with them. Familiar people begin hesitating before a name; an old joke receives a polite smile from someone who once told it.
philosophy.at_the_table: Let a former guest seek proof of a rescue so they can reclaim an ordinary place in a household. The witnesses want to help but cannot agree whom they remember. Do not make remaining permanently unbound the only valid outcome.
